rationale: C07 is a highly persuasive drafting parent. It addresses the same proposed increase in compensation for senior federal executives and supplies the child’s central argument, including the recruiting-and-retention problem, comparison with rising government and private-sector salaries, the legislation’s small cost relative to gains in efficiency, and the concluding appeal that Congress provide the President with the means to obtain and retain qualified officials. The child updates and expands this earlier appeal after the legislation advanced in Congress. C08 shares the same recipient and a similar letter structure for urging favorable Senate action, but its subject and substantive arguments are different. C16 is a weaker example of the general legislative-advocacy form.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the efficient administration of the Executive Branch of the Government requires well qualified people for important positions. Because of the inadequate salaries provided for these positions, it has become increasingly difficult for me to get and keep such people.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Inadequate salaries have long made it difficult to obtain and hold able men for positions of greatest responsibility in the Government service.
shared_material.explanation: Both make inadequate executive salaries the cause of difficulty recruiting and retaining qualified senior officials.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Salaries and wages in private industry have also been greatly increased in recent years, while no corresponding increase has been made in the salaries of Federal executives.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In the meantime, other salaries, in both government and industry, have risen sharply, and opportunities for larger compensation in private industry have greatly expanded.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely reuses the comparison between stagnant senior federal salaries and increases elsewhere in government and private industry.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The relatively small cost of this legislation will be repaid many times over in improved efficiency in the operation of the Government.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Its small cost will be repaid many times.
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, nearly verbatim language supporting the same legislation with the same cost-benefit argument.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I urge the Senate to act favorably upon this legislation, which will do so much to help me in properly discharging the duties of my office.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I ask the Congress to give me the means which will make it possible for me to get and keep the men who are required for the job ahead.
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude with a personal presidential appeal that passage is necessary to staff and administer the executive branch effectively.
